result.name: ～た　ことが　ある
result.connection: Vた + ことがある ことがない ことがあります ことがありません

examples.jp: この歌は聞いたことがあります。
examples.vi: Tôi từng nghe bài hát này.

examples.jp: 富士山に登ったことがありますか。
examples.vi: Anh đã bao giờ leo núi Phú Sĩ chưa.
examples.tr: Have you ever climbed Mt. Fuji?

examples.jp: わたしは高校生のとき、１年間アメリカで勉強したことがあります。
examples.vi: Khi còn học cấp 3, tôi đã từng học ở Mỹ 1 năm.
examples.tr: When I was in high school, I studied in America for a year.

examples.jp: 「この歌を知っていますか」「はい、前に一度聞いたことがあります」
examples.vi: “Bạn có biết bài hát này không?” “Vâng, trước đây tôi đã từng nghe một lần.”
examples.tr: “Do you know this song?” “Yes, I've heard it once before.”

examples.jp: わたしはまだ一度も雪を見たことがありません。
examples.vi: Tôi vẫn chưa từng thấy tuyết dù chỉ một lần.
examples.tr: I have never seen snow, not even once.

examples.jp: 富士山に登ったことがある？
examples.vi: Bạn đã từng leo núi Phú Sĩ chưa?
examples.tr: Have you ever climbed Mt. Fuji?

result.explain:
Often used with words indicating the number of times:一度／何回も／数回／一回も…ない to make clear how often the experience happened.
Polite form: 〜たことが あります ／〜たことが ありません .
When asking about experience: 〜たことが ありますか ？ is the polite, neutral pattern.

• Vたことがある expresses a past experience without a specific point in time, focusing on “whether one has ever done it or not”.
• Negative: Vたことがない = has never had that experience at all.
• Not used with very specific events/clear points in time (昨日/先週…), because that contradicts its “non-specific time” nature.
• Different from plain Vた: Vた tells of something that happened once (a time may be given); Vたことがある emphasizes the experience of having done it.

rows: <ruby>寿司<rt>すし</rt></ruby>を<ruby>食<rt>た</rt></ruby>べたことがある
Can be tied to a specific point in time
<ruby>昨日<rt>きのう</rt></ruby><ruby>寿司<rt>すし</rt></ruby>を<ruby>食<rt>た</rt></ruby>べた
<ruby>留学<rt>りゅうがく</rt></ruby>の<ruby>経験<rt>けいけん</rt></ruby>がある

mistakes: Attaching a specific point in time: “昨日富士山に登ったことがある” (unnatural) → “昨日登った” or “富士山に登ったことがある”.
Confusing it with habit: “よく行く” ≠ “行ったことがある”. One is frequent, the other is an experience one has had.
Dropping こと is inappropriate in formal written language: “食べたことある” is colloquial; the JLPT requires the full form.
Incorrect double negative: “一度も行ったことありません” (correct), not “一度も行ったことないです” in standard exam language (keep the level of politeness consistent).
result.notes:
• Adding a broad time frame is still fine: 子どものころに、海外へ行ったことがある (childhood, not a specific point in time).
• With もう/まだ: もう行ったことがあります (have already been)／まだ行ったことがありません (have still never been).
• In natural conversation, ことが is often omitted: 食べたことある？ (colloquial).
